notes: The handwritten page number is 32 followed by a point. The upper portion argues the two inclusions needed for F\setminus G=F′\setminus G′. The second inclusion uses a least containing member A of F and an equality of open strata. The side note reads “va se simplifier, cf plus bas”. A largely cancelled attempt at b)⇒c) follows; a new b⇔c paragraph introduces the common open support U and open subsets of ordered index sets. The sheet stops after “On a”. No title or date occurs.

After “prouvons que A′=A”, the parenthesis clearly says “d’où A∈F”, with no prime. A was already chosen in F. The conclusion that would finish the announced goal is A′∈F; it follows by substitution from A′=A and A∈F (033-check-01), but the transcription keeps the unprimed A. H supplies the expected prime and thereby removes the written slip.

The interlinear clause reads “il suffirait F′≪F”, not H’s i.e. sachant. The text invokes “cf lemme plus bas” for the equality of strata. The lemma is not proved within the supplied end of this page, so no full proof check of the second inclusion or the b/c equivalence is claimed. The two “absurde” conclusions and “qed” are the author’s own proof markers, not certifications by this edition.

The two formulas after the least-element choice have a common lower bracket with upturned ends and two worked-over raised marks on A. The first heavily retraced relation remains subset/membership doubtful. After the lemma reference, the words et bien are visible; bien is preferred as live and underlined but a low cancellation remains possible. The cancelled glyph before A,A′ has a left stem and rightward bars favoring F; H’s right-stem existential quantifier is not supported.

All long oblique cancellations in the lower attempt stop above its final “Prouvons A′^{circ(F′)}=A^{circ(F)}” sentence. The edition therefore prefers that last sentence as live, while retaining a whole-paragraph cancellation as an explicit state alternative. The earlier insertion On suppose is itself crossed with the abandoned passage; H records this accurately in an editorial note. A curved insertion leader before Soit is not a textual parenthesis.

At the bottom, the two raised glyphs on I and I′ are alike and both retain star/k/plus/left-arrow doubt. The densely overwritten difference sign is not regularized. The identification written (=F) has a looped upper arm that also admits P; F remains preferred, without using the expected index identification to settle the letter. The comma after U, the abbreviation ens without a point, and the unmatched outer parenthesis before parties are retained.

The blind pass recovered the live implication arrow before 1°), omitted by both witnesses and the first consolidated reading. The cancelled lower argument reads est un followed by an abbreviated str.t-ouvert-like form and pour; the first expansion to une strate ouverte … de was withdrawn. The abbreviated form and intervening hatched glyph remain doubtful. At the right edge of the upper bracketed pair, the exponent is clipped; a closing parenthesis formerly supplied is no longer transcribed. These are ink decisions, not mathematical repairs.

check_events.outcome: The local intended conclusion A′∈F follows immediately by substitution from the stated A′=A and the earlier choice A∈F. The written parenthesis has unprimed A∈F. This checks only the substitution/target mismatch, not existence of the least containing member or the equality of strata.
